headline.purpose: The section title at the top of each assessment section, in Slate Teal. Largest type that ships.

title.purpose: Person name, card group headings, empty-state titles, logotype.

body.purpose: Product default: rail items, card text, read values, alert copy.

control.purpose: Every input, textarea and select. One step above body so the thing being typed into stays legible on a tablet.

label.purpose: Field labels above the control, never floating inside it.

micro.purpose: Metadata, hints, errors, badge text, secondary counts.

group-label.purpose: Uppercase label for a structural region (rail head, evidence column, panel heading). Never an editorial kicker above a heading.

shadows.name: resting-sheet
shadows.purpose: Default. Cards and primary buttons resting on the oat ground.

shadows.name: rail-edge
shadows.purpose: Inset hairline where a rail meets content.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input focus halo, paired with a Deep Sea border shift. The system's only zero-offset shadow.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The product's only easing curve. Exponential ease-out on every state change.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and shadow transitions on buttons, rail items and input focus.

motion.name: settle-in
motion.value: settle-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px) } to { opacity: 1; transform: none }
motion.purpose: Evidence entries arriving in place rather than appearing from nowhere.

motion.name: pulse-soft
motion.purpose: Skeleton loading rows. Skeletons, never a centred spinner.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All motion is suppressed product-wide. Non-negotiable.

narrative.overview:
CareFrame is a workspace that behaves like a well-kept paper case file opened flat on a kitchen table: a warm oat ground, white working sheets laid on it, hairline rules instead of boxes, and a tab edge down the left that tells you where you are in the record. Nothing is glossy, nothing floats, nothing asks for attention it has not earned. The register is clinical but domestic — this is at-home care, not a hospital console — which is why the neutral channel is warm oat rather than grey, and why the brand teal is a full-height field of colour on the rail rather than a decorative accent dropped on a white dashboard.

The organising conviction is evidential. The three-column shell — Slate Teal rail (232px), white work surface with a 760px field column, oat evidence column (340px) — exists so that what the record raises sits physically beside the field that raised it. Risk is a layer riding over the terrain in one reserved ink; it never recolours the fields beneath it. People are marked in Dusty Mulberry and nowhere else. Section state is a printed mark on a hairline — hairline at rest, filled when done, struck when skipped — because a list of marks reads as a record and a row of pills reads as a dashboard.

Density is high but unhurried. Body type is 14px with generous 22px leading, controls are 16px so they survive a tablet in bad lamplight, and all numerals are tabular. The build is light-only by decision: the use scene is daytime home visits and PDF output, and there is no dark mode to maintain across eleven section forms. Motion is state-only, 150–220ms on an exponential ease-out, and is fully suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion. There is no page-load choreography anywhere in the build.
keyCharacteristics: Warm oat ground (#FAF8F4) with white work surfaces and 1px oat hairlines, never grey
Slate Teal left rail as a full-height field of colour, not a tinted sidebar
Mulberry reserved exclusively for named human beings in the record
One typeface, Public Sans, self-hosted, on a fixed rem scale at a ~1.2 ratio
Low offset shadows only; never a zero-offset halo
Light-only, tabular numerals, one focus ring product-wide

rules.name: The Mulberry Is People Rule
rules.body: Dusty Mulberry marks a named human being in the record and nothing else. If what you are colouring is a state, a status, a count, a category or a chart series, it is not mulberry. Audit test: point at any mulberry pixel and name the person it belongs to; if you cannot, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Green Channel Is Taken Rule
rules.body: The brand occupies the green channel, so Low risk is neutral oat — not green — and "saved / in progress" is carried by brand teal. Green remains reserved for the clinical success state only. Low risk should not shout; a quiet badge is the correct answer.

rules.name: The Colour Is Never Alone Rule
rules.body: No status is communicated by hue alone. Every risk badge carries an icon and a word; every alert carries an icon and a title. A screenshot rendered in greyscale must still be readable by a clinician.

rules.name: The Clinical Hues Don't Drift Rule
rules.body: green, red, orange and yellow stay exactly as Tailwind ships them. They were deliberately not warmed when the brand was. Do not harmonise them.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Public Sans does everything. There is no display face, no serif accent, no second sans. Hierarchy comes from the fixed rem scale, weight (400/500/600) and ink colour. Do not introduce a second family to make something feel important.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on body product-wide. NHS numbers, dates, phone numbers and counts align in columns and do not jitter as they change. Do not override it.

rules.name: The No Decorative Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Uppercase 0.6875rem type labels a region (a rail, a column, a panel). It never sits above a heading as an editorial kicker or eyebrow. If a heading needs a line above it to be understood, the heading is wrong.

rules.name: The Three-Column Thesis Rule
rules.body: The evidence column is not a sidebar that can be dropped on small screens. It reflows inline beneath the fields and keeps every entry's "raised in" provenance link. Never replace it with a floating help button, a modal or a drawer.

rules.name: The No Halo Rule
rules.body: Every elevation shadow carries a vertical offset and a cool-charcoal tint (rgb(31 28 24 / …)). A zero-offset, evenly-spread shadow is a glow, and the only legitimate glow in this system is the focus ring. No hard offset shadows, no coloured drop shadows.

dos: Do use the named brand / teal / oat / mulberry scales and the React primitives in components/ui for all new work.
Do keep Dusty Mulberry #8F5C72 for named human beings only — carers, next of kin, relationships, avatars.
Do render Low risk as neutral oat and "saved / in progress" as brand teal; the green channel belongs to the brand.
Do pair every status colour with an icon and a word.
Do express section state as a printed mark on a hairline — hairline at rest, filled when done, struck when skipped.
Do keep controls at 16px and body at 14px, and leave tabular numerals on.
Do separate regions with 1px Oat Rule hairlines and tonal steps (oat ground → white → oat recessed).
Do keep motion to state changes at 150–220ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), and leave the prefers-reduced-motion suppression intact.
Do self-host type; a care record makes no third-party font request.
Do carry every evidence entry with the field that produced it.
donts: Don't use mulberry for a system state, status, category or chart series.
Don't soften, warm or re-tint green / red / orange / yellow; they carry clinical meaning.
Don't add a dark mode or dark-mode variants. Light-only is a decision, not an omission.
Don't add a second typeface, a display face, or a system display font. Public Sans is the whole voice.
Don't use a zero-offset or hard-offset shadow for elevation; offset-and-tinted only, and the focus ring is the sole glow.
Don't remove or restyle the product's single focus ring.
Don't replace the section rail's marks with a row of filled pills (the sub-1024px tab strip is the one exception, and it is a tab strip).
Don't put an uppercase kicker or eyebrow line above a heading; the 0.6875rem uppercase style labels regions only.
Don't reach for stock blue-* / gray-* / purple-* / indigo-* classes in new code. They are remapped to brand ramps as a safety net for unmigrated markup, not as an API.
Don't convert existing .cf-* section-form markup to the React primitives as a drive-by; that boundary is deliberate and the field wiring is load-bearing.
Don't add page-load choreography, entrance animations or scroll-triggered reveals.
